title: EATF AEP v1 metadata.json
description: Validates the metadata.json entry inside an AEP v1 evidence package. Wire format documented in docs/aep-profile.md. The signature, timestamp, and OVERT-inspired receipt are validated by the verifier separately; this schema only constrains metadata.json.

schema.description: Schema identifier URN. Optional in v0.1 for backwards compatibility with sparse early metadata payloads; when present MUST equal 'urn:eatf:spec:aep:metadata:1.0'.

attestation_id.description: Globally unique identifier for this attestation. Producers are encouraged to use a ULID, UUIDv7, or another monotonically-sortable scheme.

tenant_id_hash.description: SHA-256 hex of the deployment-local tenant identifier; or all-zeros for fixtures. Optional.

agent_id.description: URN identifier of the agent producing the attestation. Conventional form: urn:eatf:tenant:<tenant>:agent:<slug>.

action_type.description: Free-form classifier of the action being attested, e.g. 'mcp.tools/call:github.create_issue' or 'foundational:llm-response'.

model.description: Identifier of the model that produced the underlying response (when applicable).

policy_id.description: Identifier of the policy under which the action was evaluated.

policy_coverage.description: Fraction of policy rules that successfully evaluated (1.0 means full coverage).

policy_decision.description: Policy outcome for the recorded action.

warrant_id.description: Identifier of the warrant.json entry carried in the same package. Optional; present when the package carries a warrant.

warrant_version.description: Version string of the packaged warrant.

warrant_digest.description: Lower-case hex SHA-256 of warrant.json as packaged (its JCS-canonical bytes). Binds the warrant to this package; under the profile canonical form this field sits inside the signed canonical bytes.

voiding.description: Optional array of typed per-output voiding predicates (docs/specs/aep-profile-v1.md section 4.4). Each entry is a machine-evaluable condition that, when it holds, voids or degrades the output. Verifiers evaluate every predicate at verify time against caller-supplied inputs (a dated registry snapshot, a supersession list) and emit a four-valued verdict per entry (holds / voided / unknown / not-assessed); an unknown type MUST yield not-assessed, never holds. Informational in this release: a voided verdict does not by itself fail verification.

id.description: Stable identifier of this voiding predicate within the package.

type.description: Predicate type. Determines which subject fields and which caller-supplied input the verifier consults.

subject.description: Type-specific subject of the predicate (e.g. { entry_id } for registry-status, { artifact_id } for artifact-supersession, { sampled_at, max_age_seconds } for telemetry-freshness).

on_true.description: Effect when the predicate holds: fully void the output, or degrade it.

authorizing_principal.description: Optional per-output DEONTIC authorizing principal (docs/specs/aep-profile-v1.md section 4.5): the authority that granted the subject agent a mandate to act. Distinct from the epistemic accepting_authority (who accepted that outputs under this policy license their action class). The block has two states. Named WITHOUT mandate_digest and without a packaged mandate.json, it is the REFERENCE form: no signed mandate is claimed, the verifier reports every mandate check as not determinate, and nothing about the grant is verified. With mandate_digest, or with a mandate.json entry packaged, a SIGNED mandate is claimed and the section 4.5 binding family gates verification: digest, record, binding to the protected bytes, and the granting authority's detached signature. A named principal under the same self-attestation trust model as public_key.pem; nothing here establishes it as a legally constituted authority, and whether the grant is lawful is attested, never machine-checked.

principal.description: Named principal identifier of the deontic authorizing principal (the mandate granter).

token_ref.description: Optional opaque reference to the mandate/authorization token held in the mandate layer. Not resolved or validated by this verifier.

mandate_ref.description: Identifier of the mandate-layer record. When a signed mandate is claimed, it MUST equal the packaged record's mandate_id; in the reference form it is an opaque string the verifier does not resolve.

mandate_digest.description: Binds a packaged mandate.json to this output: 'sha256:' followed by the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) bytes of mandate.json. Present only when a signed mandate is claimed. Under the profile canonical form this reference sits inside the signed canonical bytes; a claimed mandate under the response-only form is rejected, because there the reference is itself rewritable.

accepting_authority.description: Optional per-output epistemic accepting authority (docs/specs/aep-profile-v1.md section 4.3): the named principal that accepted, once, that outputs under this policy version license their action class. Distinct from the deontic authorizing principal (who granted the mandate to act). A named principal with a verifiable key binding under the same self-attestation trust model as public_key.pem; nothing here establishes it as a legally constituted authority. When a detached acceptance.json is packaged, acceptance_digest binds it. Under the profile canonical form this block sits inside the signed canonical bytes; under the response-only form it is unsigned and rewritable, so the acceptance is bound to nothing and verification FAILS. The section 4.3 binding family gates: output binding and key binding decide validity, while temporal containment and role are appraisal and are reported without rejecting.

principal.description: Named principal identifier of the accepting authority.

policy_id.description: Policy identifier this acceptance is made against; MUST equal metadata.policy_id.

policy_version.description: Policy version this acceptance is made against; MUST equal metadata.policy_version.

acceptance_digest.description: sha256:<lower-case hex> of acceptance.json as packaged (its JCS-canonical bytes), present when a detached acceptance.json / acceptance.sig pair is carried.

validity.description: Acceptance validity window. The RFC 3161 genTime is checked for containment; a genTime outside the window is reported and does not by itself fail verification.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp asserting when the producer sealed the package. The trusted timestamp in timestamp.tsr is authoritative; this field is informational.

privacy_mode.description: Whether the underlying response is included verbatim (false) or only its hash (true).

mcp.description: Optional MCP-specific block for tools/call attestations.
